title: 2026: The Year The IDE Died — Steve Yegge & Gene Kim, Authors, Vibe Coding
talk_summary: A keynote arguing that single-agent CLI tools like Claude Code are the wrong architecture because every request hits the expensive model and one context window is a single oxygen tank; the fix is task decomposition into many specialized agents (PM, coder, reviewer, tester, merge) coordinated through markdown/APIs. It also reports that trust in AI tools grows with hours of use, and that high code velocity forces one-engineer-per-repo because merge-conflict coordination cost is unsolved.

takeaways.technique: Decompose into role-specialized agents instead of one big-context agent
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of giving one agent a huge context window, split the work across a pipeline of narrow agents (product manager, coder, reviewer, tester, merge) each with its own small context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you should send a product manager diver down first, and then a coding diver, right? And then a review diver, and a test diver, and a Git merge diver

takeaways.technique: Route cheap questions away from the expensive model
takeaways.what_they_do: Critique that CLI agents send every request, including trivial ones, to the top-tier model, wasting quota.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If I say, "Is my Git ignore file still there?" I've also gone to the expensive model, right? Everything that you say goes to the expensive model.

takeaways.technique: Fix small issues on the spot instead of backlog grooming
takeaways.what_they_do: When a customer issue appears, fix and ship it immediately rather than filing it to a backlog and arguing in grooming.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of putting them on a Jira backlog and, you know, arguing with about it in the grooming sessions ... We just fix it on the spot

takeaways.technique: One owner per repo to avoid merge-conflict coordination cost
takeaways.what_they_do: At very high code velocity they concluded only one engineer can work a repo at a time because merge conflicts and coordination cost dominate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our code velocity is so high, uh we've both concluded that we can only have one engineer per repo, right? Because of merge conflicts

takeaways.what_they_do: DORA data shows trust in AI tools rises with length of use, implying skill is teachable and short trials are misleading.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the longer you use AI, right? The more you trust it, right?

takeaways.technique: AI-generated PRs rejected as slop when labeled
takeaways.what_they_do: A team rejected a PR when told it was AI-generated but accepted the same fix when not labeled, showing label bias in human review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Unlike the time when they said it was AI generated and they rejected it as AI slop, right?
